subject: Cost and Management Accounting
question_html: According to the Study Material, the main cause of inaccuracy in a traditional costing system lies in-

options.A: the incorrect classification of direct materials and direct wages
options.B: the calculation of the overhead rate itself, which is usually based on direct labour hours or machine hours
options.C: the failure to spread service centre overheads over production cost centres
options.D: the use of pre-determined rates instead of actual rates of overhead absorption

answer_html:
Answer: (B) the calculation of the overhead rate itself, which is usually based on direct labour hours or machine hours.

Some traditional systems do treat overheads in a detailed way and relate them to service as well as production cost centres. The main cause of inaccuracy is in the calculation of the overhead rate itself, which is usually based on direct labour hours or machine hours.

subject: Cost and Management Accounting
question_html: Overhead rates based on direct labour hours or machine hours implicitly assume that-

options.A: all products consume the same amount of direct material
options.B: products that take longer to make generate more overheads
options.C: overheads are wholly fixed in nature and do not respond to activity
options.D: each product is produced in batches of an identical size

answer_html:
Answer: (B) products that take longer to make generate more overheads.

Rates based on direct labour hours or machine hours assume that products which take longer to make generate more overheads. Where a significant part of the overhead is driven by non-volume related activities, this assumption produces inaccurate product costs.

subject: Cost and Management Accounting
question_html: Which of the following is NOT listed as a factor that led to the development of Activity Based Costing?

options.C: Increasing product diversity to secure economies of scope and increased market share
options.D: Rising costs of information processing due to the growing complexity of computer systems

answer_html:
Answer: (D) Rising costs of information processing due to the growing complexity of computer systems.

The four factors listed are growing overhead costs because of increasingly automated production, increasing market competition, increasing product diversity, and DECREASING costs of information processing because of continual improvements and the increasing application of information technology.

question_html: Increasingly automated production has led to the development of ABC mainly because it-

options.B: causes overhead costs to grow, making their accurate assignment more important
options.C: makes direct labour hours a more reliable basis for absorbing overheads
options.D: eliminates the need for any form of overhead absorption

answer_html:
Answer: (B) causes overhead costs to grow, making their accurate assignment more important.

One of the factors prompting the development of ABC is growing overhead costs because of increasingly automated production. As overheads form a larger share of total cost, the accuracy of the method used to assign them becomes far more important.

question_html: Decreasing costs of information processing have contributed to the development of ABC because-

answer_html:
Answer: (A) they permit the detailed data collection and analysis that an activity based system requires.

Decreasing costs of information processing, because of continual improvements and the increasing application of information technology, is one of the four factors that led to the development of ABC, since ABC depends on far more detailed data than a traditional system.

subject: Cost and Management Accounting
question_html: Activity Based Costing is described in the Study Material as-

options.C: a method of valuing closing inventory at net realisable value
options.D: a system that dispenses with the absorption of overheads altogether

question_html: When an organisation faces stiff competition and urgently needs to compute cost accurately and fix the selling price according to the market situation, ABC is-

question_html: Based on the stated usefulness and limitations of ABC, in which of the following situations would ABC be LEAST appropriate?

options.B: A company facing stiff competition which prices its products on a cost-plus basis

subject: Cost and Management Accounting
question_html: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the two categories of cost driver?

options.A: A resource cost driver measures the quantity of resources consumed by an activity and assigns resource cost to an activity cost pool; an activity cost driver measures the frequency and intensity of demand placed on activities by cost objects and assigns activity cost to cost objects
options.B: A resource cost driver assigns activity costs to cost objects; an activity cost driver assigns resource costs to activity cost pools

answer_html:

A resource cost driver is a measure of the quantity of resources consumed by an activity and is used to assign the cost of a resource to an activity or cost pool. An activity cost driver is a measure of the frequency and intensity of demand placed on activities by cost objects, and is used to assign activity costs to cost objects.

subject: Cost and Management Accounting
question_html: Which of the following correctly describes the first stage of cost allocation under the two systems?

options.A: In traditional absorption costing overheads are first related to activities, whereas in ABC they are first related to cost centres
options.B: In traditional absorption costing overheads are first related to cost centres (production and service centres), whereas in ABC they are related to activities or grouped into cost pools

answer_html:
Answer: (B) In traditional absorption costing overheads are first related to cost centres (production and service centres), whereas in ABC they are related to activities or grouped into cost pools.

In traditional absorption costing, overheads are first related to cost centres (production and service centres) and then to cost objects, that is, products. In ABC, overheads are related to activities or grouped into cost pools and then related to the cost objects. The two processes are very similar, but the first stage is different.

subject: Cost and Management Accounting
question_html: A company's overheads of ₹11,250 are analysed into three pools: ₹4,500 driven by direct labour hours, ₹2,500 driven by machine hours and ₹4,250 driven by the number of purchase orders. Total labour hours are 1,000, machine hours 250 and purchase orders 100. The cost driver rate per purchase order is-
answer_html:
Answer: (C) ₹42.50.

The cost driver rate is the total cost in the activity pool divided by the base. For purchase orders, ₹4,250 / 100 orders = ₹42.50 per purchase order. The other two rates are ₹4,500 / 1,000 = ₹4.50 per labour hour and ₹2,500 / 250 = ₹10 per machine hour.

subject: Cost and Management Accounting
question_html: ABC is stated to aid cost control, whereas traditional absorption costing is said to be not suitable for cost control, because-

subject: Cost and Management Accounting
question_html: The problem with using functional departments as the first-stage collection point, which ABC overcomes by using activities, is that functional departments-

subject: Cost and Management Accounting
question_html: Where a company using direct labour hours as the overhead application base switches to ABC and finds that a substantial part of its overhead is driven by orders processed and inspections, the typical finding on cost distortion is that-

options.A: the low volume product is under-costed and the high volume product is over-costed under the direct labour hour basis
options.B: the low volume product is over-costed and the high volume product is under-costed under the direct labour hour basis
options.C: both products are under-costed under the direct labour hour basis
options.D: neither product is distorted, since the total overhead absorbed is the same under both systems

answer_html:
Answer: (A) the low volume product is under-costed and the high volume product is over-costed under the direct labour hour basis.

A volume-based rate spreads overhead in proportion to labour hours, so it charges too little to products that make heavy demands on non-volume related activities. As the Study Material's illustration shows, the low volume product is under-costed and the high volume product is over-costed when direct labour hours are used for overhead absorption.

subject: Cost and Management Accounting
question_html: Where activity cost rates are computed on the basis of cost driver capacity rather than actual usage, the cost of unused capacity for an activity is measured as-

options.A: the whole of the activity cost, since none of it can be assigned to products
options.B: the unused quantity of the cost driver multiplied by the activity cost rate
options.C: the actual quantity of the cost driver consumed multiplied by the activity cost rate
options.D: nil, because activity costs are always fully absorbed by the products

answer_html:
Answer: (B) the unused quantity of the cost driver multiplied by the activity cost rate.

When rates are based on cost driver capacity, only the drivers actually consumed are charged to products. The balance, that is, the unused quantity of the cost driver multiplied by the activity cost rate, is the cost of unused capacity, which is reported separately rather than loaded on to product cost.

subject: Cost and Management Accounting
case_facts_html:
Nova Ltd. manufactures two products, EX and WY, and at present absorbs production overheads on the basis of direct labour hours. Budgeted production overheads for the period are ₹9,00,000 and budgeted direct labour hours are 30,000. Product EX: 5,000 units, 4 direct labour hours per unit. Product WY: 2,500 units, 4 direct labour hours per unit.

The company now proposes to adopt Activity Based Costing. The budgeted overheads have been analysed into three activity cost pools: machine set-up ₹3,00,000 (driver: number of set-ups), order processing ₹2,40,000 (driver: number of purchase orders) and machine operation ₹3,60,000 (driver: machine hours).

Cost driver data - set-ups: EX 20, WY 80 (total 100); purchase orders: EX 40, WY 160 (total 200); machine hours: EX 9,000, WY 3,000 (total 12,000).
question_html: What is the production overhead absorbed per unit of Product EX under the existing direct labour hour basis?
answer_html:
Answer: (B) ₹120.00.

Overhead absorption rate = ₹9,00,000 / 30,000 direct labour hours = ₹30 per hour. Product EX uses 4 hours per unit, so the overhead per unit = 4 x ₹30 = ₹120. Since both products use 4 hours per unit, the traditional system charges each of them the same ₹120.
